card.name: Yumbada
card.era: Pre-Hispanic origins; present Cotocollao ritual revived ~20 years ago
card.tagline: Indigenous ritual dance-drama of forest 'yumbos' near Quito.
card.profile: The Yumbada is an Indigenous (Kichwa) and mestizo ritual dance-drama performed in neighborhoods of Quito, most prominently Cotocollao and La Magdalena, each June around Corpus Christi and the solstice (Casa de la Cultura Ecuatoriana). Dancers personify 'yumbos,' shaman figures associated with the Amazonian/montane forest, led by a 'mamaco' or pingullero who plays a small drum and a three-note pingullo flute. The ritual climax is the 'Yumbo Huanuchiy' (Killing of the Yumbo), a dramatized murder and resurrection linked to healing, fertility and the mythic alliance of the Quitu and Cara peoples (Frank Salomon, IFEA; El Telegrafo). Dancers carry black chonta-palm lances and wear long wigs, ribbons, plumes and masks; it is treated as a sacred rite rather than folkloric spectacle.
card.insight: Anthropologist Frank Salomon documented the Yumbada as a ritual drama; four yumbadas coexist today in Quito's Zona La Delicia (Rumicucho, Pomasqui, Tanlahua, Cotocollao), and the Cotocollao community pursued, then withdrew from, formal national heritage declaration, fearing folklorization (Salomon, IFEA; Quito Informa).
card.image_significance: Ceremonial yumbo dance-drama. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Quito area, Ecuador.
